text: First, your sleep is more important than anything. With your dog being a small fragile breed, he should NEVER be jumping off or onto a bed/couch, etc. The short legs give less time to absorb the impact, therefore causing higher risk for knee, wrist, elbow and back injury. A good gage to go by is the height of any object for jumping onto or off of should be no higher than the length of your dog, minus tail & head.This does not apply to puppies, senior dogs dogs, long back breeds (dachshund, Shiztu, etc) or any "delicate " breed. After he and you are deemed healthy, i would start with a small wire crate in the living room. Leave door open at all times. Cover with thin blanket and place extra cushy, soft bedding inside. We want this to be a place he "wants" to go. After set up, give "high value" treat, like a piece of plain chicken to entice him to explore. Do this for a week or 2 until he grows accustomed to his own little man cave. We want him to go in regularly because he likes it, not because he gets a treat. You can slowly cut the treat to a tiny piece, then just affection after he goes in. In other words, his crate becomes a very inviting, positive place. I suggest as others have said, exercise him as much as possible 1 hour before your bedtime. BTW, dogs typically do not rationalize. He will not be wondering why he is not in your bed at night. This my opinion after working for a veterinarian for 26 years. Good luck sweetie. Keep us posted.

text: Honestly, 30k can be enough if you’re careful. I don’t make a ton either, and I’ve had my dog for years. The monthly stuff — food, treats, basic vet — is totally doable on a budget.
